name: MEDAS
shortDescription: 14-item PREDIMED screener measuring adherence to a cardiovascular-protective Mediterranean diet (higher is better).
timeframe: Thinking about your typical eating habits over the past few weeks, answer Yes or No to each dietary criterion:
citation: Schröder H, Fitó M, Estruch R, et al. J Nutr. 2011;141(6):1140-1145.

questions.text: Do you use olive oil as your main culinary fat?
Do you consume 4 or more tablespoons of olive oil in a given day (including frying, salads, and meals eaten away from home)?
Do you consume 2 or more servings of vegetables per day (1 serving ≈ 200 g / 1 cup cooked or 2 cups raw, with at least 1 portion raw or as salad)?
Do you consume 3 or more fruit units per day (including freshly squeezed natural fruit juices)?
Do you consume less than 1 serving of red meat, hamburger, or meat products (ham, sausage, etc.) per day (1 serving ≈ 100–150 g)?
Do you consume less than 1 serving of butter, margarine, or cream per day (1 serving ≈ 12 g / 1 tablespoon)?
Do you consume less than 1 sweet or carbonated sugar-sweetened beverage per day?
Do you drink 7 or more glasses of wine per week? (Original PREDIMED item — see clinical note below)
Do you consume 3 or more servings of legumes (beans, lentils, chickpeas) per week (1 serving ≈ 150 g cooked)?
Do you consume 3 or more servings of fish or shellfish per week (1 serving ≈ 100–150 g fish or 4–5 pieces shellfish)?
Do you consume commercial sweets or pastries (not homemade), such as cakes, cookies, biscuits, or custard, fewer than 3 times per week?
Do you consume 3 or more servings of nuts (including peanuts) per week (1 serving ≈ 30 g / a small handful)?
Do you preferentially consume chicken, turkey, or rabbit meat instead of veal, pork, hamburger, or sausage?
Do you consume vegetables, pasta, rice, or other dishes seasoned with sofrito (sauce made with tomato and onion, leek, or garlic simmered in olive oil) 2 or more times per week?

scoring.formulaDescription: Count of met criteria across all 14 items (range 0–14). Per PREDIMED (Schröder et al., 2011), scores ≤5 indicate low adherence, 6–9 moderate adherence, and ≥10 high adherence. Clinical note: while original PREDIMED Q8 awards 1 point for ≥7 glasses of wine/week, current WHO & AHA guidance recognizes no risk-free level of alcohol — non-drinkers should not begin drinking to increase this score.
